items.t: CVT overheats, loses power or fails
items.job: Replace CVT with a remanufactured or used unit
items.note: CarComplaints owners report about $1,100 for overheating repairs and $2,500-$3,200 for failures. Fluid service alone costs far less.

items.job: Clear and reseat sunroof drain tubes; reseal roof seams

items.t: Engine stalls from crankshaft sensor or throttle body faults
items.job: Replace crankshaft position sensor or electronic throttle body
items.note: Owners report a typical bill of about $660; a throttle body is the high end.

items.t: Underhood fuse and relay box (TIPM) failure
Front and rear crossmembers can rust through (warranty extension X69)
items.note: May be covered by Chrysler's 10-year X69 extension; ask a dealer.

items.t: Worn control arms, sway bar links and tie rod ends
items.job: Replace front lower control arms and tie rod ends, then align

items.t: Check engine light for oxygen sensor codes (TSB)
Engine computer may crack and stall the engine (recall)
Seatbelt tensioner and side airbag timing error (recall)
Airbag control module may short out (recall)
Steering column rivet may be missing (recall)
items.job: Inspect and repair steering column pivot rivet

items.t: Fuel transfer tube may cause stalling (recall)
Balance shaft debris can cut oil pressure (recall)
Power steering return hose can come off (recall)
Crank or cam sensor connector may stall the engine (recall)
items.job: Replace crank or cam sensor connector
Replace alternator (worn bearing or decoupler pulley)
items.note: YourMechanic: $849 estimate for most 2007–2015 years ($1,075 for 2016); its average is $525 ($315 parts, $210 labor). Shop/dealer range about $1,010–$1,935. Replacing only the decoupler pulley costs less. No parts-plus-labor source with book hours was found, so this is based on YourMechanic.

items.t: ABS light from wheel bearing, sensor or wiring faults
items.note: YourMechanic: $187–$334 per sensor (front sensors cost more), averaging $46 parts and $95 labor. RepairPal ABS inspection for a 2016: $413–$510. A worn wheel bearing or corroded wiring costs more. Based on YourMechanic; no parts-plus-labor source with book hours was found.
